'''Ömer Faruk Yurtseven''' (born 19 June 1998) is a Turkish professional [[basketball]] player who most recently played for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. He plays the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position.<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Omer-Yurtseven-73269/ Ömer Faruk Yurtseven Draft Express Profile]</ref>

==Early life and career==
He was born in [[Tashkent]], Uzbekistan<ref>{{cite web|title=Omer Yurtseven|url=https://gleague.nba.com/player/omer-yurtseven/|website=NBA.com|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref> to [[Turkish people|Turkish]] parents and played basketball in Turkey and for the Turkish youth national team. He was selected to the Best Five of the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] and was also invited to play at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ömer Faruk Yurtseven, "Jordan Brand Classic" Kampına Katıldı|url=http://www.tbf.org.tr/detay/2014/04/19/%C3%B6mer-faruk-yurtseven-jordan-brand-classic-kamp%C4%B1na-kat%C4%B1ld%C4%B1|work=TBF.org.tr|access-date=1 October 2014|language=tr}}</ref>

On 20 March 2015, Yurtseven made his [[EuroLeague]] debut, in a game against [[Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]], scoring 2 points, in 1 minute and 4 seconds of playing time.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=208&seasoncode=E2014 FBUlker – EA7 match reports.]</ref>

On 5 October 2015, Yurtseven played against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], at the [[Barclays Center]], in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]]. He had 8 points and 7 rebounds, with one block, in 15 minutes and 18 seconds of playing time, in his team's win over the Nets.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150906000454/http://www.nba.com/games/20151005/FBUBKN/gameinfo.html Fenerbahce – NJN match reports.]</ref> He became the youngest player in history at the time to play in an NBA preseason game, at 17 years old.

During an under-18 youth age competition in Turkey, Yurtseven recorded a double-double, of 91 points (scoring more points than his entire competition), making 34 out of 49 shots (including five three-pointers), and grabbing 28 rebounds, in a 115–82 win over the youth club of Eylul Basketbol Ihtisas.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Jeff|last1=Goodman|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|name-list-style=and|title=NC State adds Turkish 7-footer Omer Yurtseven|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/15562724|website=ESPN.com|date=16 May 2016|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Five-star C Omer Yurtseven scores 91 points in U-18 game|url=https://www.si.com/college/2016/05/15/omer-yurtseven-recruiting-fenerbahce-91-point-game|website=SI.com|date=15 May 2016|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref>

On 15 February 2016, he left [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]], in order to play [[college basketball]], stating that he needed more playing time than he was receiving with Fenerbahçe.<ref>[https://www.haberler.com/spor/omer-faruk-yurtseven-fenerbahce-den-ayrilma-8162102-haberi/ Ömer Faruk Yurtseven: Fenerbahçe'den Ayrılma Kararı Aldım {{in lang|tr}}]</ref>

==College career==
On 16 May 2016 it was announced that Yurtseven would be playing [[college basketball]] at [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State University]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/GoodmanESPN/status/732269082628628481 N.C. State picked up Turkish 7-footer Omer Yurtseven:]</ref> However, due to his previous exposure with playing for [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]], in some [[professional sports|professional]] games, the [[NCAA]] decided to suspend him for the first nine games of their season (around 30% of the schedule), as well as require him to donate $1,000 to a charity of his choosing, in exchange for him to be fully eligible for playing time moving forward.<ref>{{cite news|first=Joe|last=Giglio|title=NC State's Omer Yurtseven cleared to play by NCAA, but must sit 9 games|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article111615327.html|work=[[Raleigh News and Observer]]|date=31 October 2016|access-date=18 November 2016}}</ref> After fulfilling his suspension, he returned to the court on December 15, in a win against [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State University]]. On 14 March 2017, Yurtseven would test out his stock for the [[2017 NBA draft]], leaving open the possibility that he would return to North Carolina State for his sophomore season. After trying out for the 2017 [[NBA Draft Combine]], his father announced he'd be going back to North Carolina State for his sophomore year.

During his sophomore year he would improve his points per game average from 5.9 to 13.5. This significant increase gained him [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] Third Team honors. On 21 March 2018, Yurtseven would test out going pro once again for the [[2018 NBA draft]]. However, even if he stayed in college, he confirmed that he would not return to North Carolina State and would instead request a transfer to a different university.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sammy|last=Batten|title=Center Omer Yurtseven leaving N.C. State|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2018/03/21/center-omer-yurtseven-leaving-nc-state/12942461007|website=FayObserver.com|date=21 March 2018|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref>

On April 16, 2018, Yurtseven announced he would transfer to [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. He became eligible to play for the Hoyas starting in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] with two years of eligibility remaining.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|title=Omer Yurtseven transferring from NC State to Georgetown|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23200531|website=ESPN.com|date=16 April 2018|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref> Yurtseven had 20 points in his debut for Georgetown, an 81–68 win over [[Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball|Mount St. Mary's]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Georgetown defeats Mount St. Mary's 81–68|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168383|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=6 November 2019|access-date=10 November 2019}}</ref> He averaged 15.5 points and 9.8 rebounds per game but missed seven games with an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ava|last=Wallace|title=Georgetown's Mac McClung will enter NBA Draft, maintain eligibility|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/03/29/georgetowns-mac-mcclung-will-enter-nba-draft-maintain-eligibility/|work=[[The Washington Post]]|date=29 March 2020|access-date=16 April 2020}}</ref> On 28 April 2020, he announced that he was entering the [[2020 NBA draft]] and was not returning to Georgetown.<ref>{{cite web|first=Stefan|last=Djordjevic|title=Omer Yurtseven declared for the draft, won't return to Georgetown|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1054407/omer-yurtseven-declared-for-the-draft-wont-return-to-georgetown/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=29 April 2020|access-date=29 April 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Blue (2021)===
After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Yurtseven signed an [[Exhibit 10]] deal with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on 8 December 2020.<ref>{{cite news|first=Joe|last=Mussatto|title=OKC Thunder reportedly signs two undrafted free agents|url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5676609/okc-thunder-reportedly-signs-two-undrafted-free-agents|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|date=19 November 2020|access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref> He was waived next day.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Sign, Waive Omer Yurtseven|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/thunder-sign-omer-yurtseven-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=9 December 2020|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref> On January 28, 2021, Yurtseven was included in roster of the [[Oklahoma City Blue]], the [[NBA G League]] affiliate of the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces 2020–21 Roster|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-2020-21-roster|website=NBA.com|date=28 January 2021|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2021–2023)===
On 14 May 2021, Yurtseven signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Beguiristain|title=Ӧmer Yurtseven Signs With HEAT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/mer-yurtseven-signs-with-heat-0521|website=NBA.com|date=14 May 2021|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref> On 1 August he joined the Heat for the [[NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Beguiristain|title=2021 Miami HEAT Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-roster-2021|website=NBA.com|date=1 August 2021|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref> and five days later re-signed with the Heat.<ref>{{cite web|first=Irene|last=Herrera|title=HEAT Re-Signs Ӧmer Yurtseven|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-resigns-omer-yurtseven|website=NBA.com|date=6 August 2021|access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref> On 26 December, Yurtseven made his first career start, putting up 16 points and 15 rebounds in a 93–83 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Walter|last=Villa|title=Undermanned Magic fall in Miami and drop to 7-27|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-sp-magic-heat-1227-20211227-nftq27q37vfafivi3xzx7ppbbe-story.html|website=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=26 December 2021|access-date=29 January 2022}}</ref> On 15 November 2022, Yurtseven underwent surgery for an impingement, [[exostosis|bone spur]], and [[stress fracture|stress reaction]] in his left ankle.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ömer Yurtseven undergoes surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/omer-yurtseven-undergoes-surgery|website=NBA.com|date=15 November 2022|access-date=14 July 2023}}</ref>

Yurtseven played in the [[2023 NBA Finals]], with the Heat being the second #8 seed in NBA history to reach the [[NBA Finals]]. The Heat lost the Finals in 5 games to the [[Denver Nuggets]].

===Utah Jazz (2023–2024)===
On 17 July 2023, Yurtseven signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Center Ömer Yurtseven|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-center-omer-yurtseven|website=NBA.com|date=17 July 2023|access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref> However, he was waived on 1 July 2024.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Rincon|title=Utah Jazz Waive Ömer Yurtseven|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-omer-yurtseven|website=NBA.com|date=1 July 2024|access-date=1 July 2024}}</ref>

===Panathinaikos (2024–2026)===
On 30 August 2024, Yurtseven signed a two-year (1+1) deal with the reigning [[EuroLeague]] and [[Greek Basketball League|Greek League]] champions [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Στα πράσινα ο Γιουρτσεβέν|url=https://www.paobc.gr/deltia-typoy/105641_sta-prasina-o-gioyrtseben|website=PAOBC.gr|date=30 August 2024|access-date=30 August 2024|language=Greek}}</ref> He joined head coach [[Ergin Ataman]]'s roster, bringing NBA experience and size to strengthen Panathinaikos' frontcourt.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panathinaikos signs Ömer Yurtseven|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1706247/panathinaikos-considering-omer-yurtseven|website=EuroHoops|date=30 August 2024|access-date=11 November 2025|language=en}}</ref> During the 2024–25 EuroLeague season, Yurtseven had a standout performance in Round 19, recording 27 points, 7 rebounds, 2 assists and 3 blocks in a 111–90 win over [[Virtus Bologna|Virtus Segafredo Bologna]], earning the EuroLeague Round 19 MVP award.<ref>{{cite web|title=EuroLeague Round 19 MVP: Ömer Yurtseven|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/euroleague-round-19-mvp-omer-yurtseven-panathinaikos|website=Sportando|date=12 February 2025|access-date=11 November 2025|language=en}}</ref> On 20 January 2025, Yurtseven suffered a right leg fracture during a Greek League derby against [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]], forcing him to miss 1–2 months of competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Yurtseven sidelined for 1-2 months with leg fracture, Ataman confirms|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/heba/1774196/yurtseven-sidelined-for-1-2-months-with-leg-fracture-ataman-confirms|website=EuroHoops|date=21 January 2025|access-date=11 November 2025|language=en}}</ref>

In the 2025–26 season, Yurtseven was ruled out with a second-degree adductor strain on 2 November 2025, an injury that was expected to keep him sidelined for approximately three weeks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ömer Yurtseven out three weeks with adductor strain|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1889111/omer-yurtseven-out-three-weeks-panathinaikos-euroleague/|website=EuroHoops|date=2 November 2025|access-date=11 November 2025|language=en}}</ref> On 28 February 2026, Panathinaikos exercised an opt-out clause in Yurtseven's contract, parting ways with the Turkish center. This roster move followed previous indications from head coach Ergin Ataman, who had hinted at potential frontcourt adjustments to accommodate the return of [[Mathias Lessort]]. With Lessort reintegrated into the rotation, Yurtseven was deemed surplus to the team’s immediate tactical requirements.[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1937805/omer-yurtseven-parts-ways-with-panathinaikos-euroleague/]

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2026)===
On 4 March 2026, Yurtseven signed with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the NBA G League.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ömer Yurtseven signs with G League’s Rio Grande Valley Vipers|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1939306/omer-yurtseven-signs-with-g-leagues-rio-grande-valley-vipers/amp/|website=EuroHoops|date=4 March 2026|access-date=5 March 2026|language=en}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2026)===
On 15 March 2026, Yurtseven signed a 10-day contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-15 |title=Warriors Sign Center Ömer Yurtseven to 10-Day Contract |url=https://warriors.com/news/warriors-sign-center-omer-yurtseven-to-10-day-contract-20260315 |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez |first=Tristi |date=2026-03-14 |title=Warriors sign Omer Yurtseven to 10-day NBA contract to fill much-needed center depth, per agents |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/omer-yurtseven-nba-contract/1923971/ |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=[[NBC Sports Bay Area]] |language=en-US}}</ref> On 25 March, Yurtseven re-signed with the Warriors on a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Warriors keeping Ömer Yurtseven with second 10-day deal|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/warriors-keeping-mer-yurtseven-second-174051974.html|access-date=April 13, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Yurtseven was a member of the junior national teams of [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]]. With Turkey's junior national teams, he played at the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|2013 FIBA Europe U16 Championship]], and at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|2014 FIBA Europe U16 Championship]], where he was named to the All-Tournament Team. He also played at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|2015 FIBA Europe U18 Championship]], where he won a silver medal, and at the [[2016 FIBA U20 European Championship|2016 FIBA Europe U20 Championship]], where he won a bronze medal, and was named to the All-Tournament Team. He finished his career with Turkey's junior national teams at the [[2017 FIBA U20 European Championship|2017 FIBA Europe U20 Championship]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180408205755/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Omer%20YURTSEVEN/pid/108692/_//players.html Omer YURTSEVEN (TUR).]</ref>
